#!/bin/sh
set -eu
exec 2>&1

READY_DIR=/run/opdbus/runit-ready
READY=$READY_DIR/netmaker-adapter-loopback
DOWNSTREAM=$READY_DIR/netmk-netclient-start
SOCKET=/var/lib/opdbus-runtime/netmaker/op-grpc-adapters.sock
PORT=50061
SOCAT=${SOCAT_BIN:-/usr/bin/socat}
HELPER=${OP_NETMK_RECONCILE:-/usr/bin/op-netmk-reconcile}
WAIT_SECONDS=${NETMK_ADAPTER_WAIT_SECONDS:-120}
CHECK_INTERVAL=${NETMK_CHECK_INTERVAL:-30}
SOCAT_PID=

cleanup() {
    rm -f "$READY" "$DOWNSTREAM"
    if [ -n "$SOCAT_PID" ] && kill -0 "$SOCAT_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
        kill "$SOCAT_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
        wait "$SOCAT_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
}
trap 'cleanup; exit 0' HUP INT TERM
rm -f "$READY" "$DOWNSTREAM"
install -d -m 0755 "$READY_DIR"
[ -x "$SOCAT" ] || { echo "missing socat: $SOCAT" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -x "$HELPER" ] || { echo "missing native reconciler: $HELPER" >&2; exit 1; }

waited=0
while [ ! -S "$SOCKET" ]; do
    [ "$waited" -lt "$WAIT_SECONDS" ] || {
        echo "timed out waiting for adapter UDS $SOCKET" >&2
        exit 1
    }
    sleep 1
    waited=$((waited + 1))
done

"$SOCAT" \
    "TCP-LISTEN:${PORT},bind=127.0.0.1,reuseaddr,fork" \
    "UNIX-CONNECT:${SOCKET}" &
SOCAT_PID=$!

waited=0
until kill -0 "$SOCAT_PID" 2>/dev/null && "$HELPER" adapter-health; do
    [ "$waited" -lt "$WAIT_SECONDS" ] || {
        echo "adapter bridge did not reach authenticated health" >&2
        cleanup
        exit 1
    }
    sleep 1
    waited=$((waited + 1))
done

stamp_tmp=$READY.$$
: >"$stamp_tmp"
mv -f "$stamp_tmp" "$READY"
echo "Netmaker adapter UDS healthy on fixed endpoint 127.0.0.1:50061"

while sleep "$CHECK_INTERVAL"; do
    if ! kill -0 "$SOCAT_PID" 2>/dev/null || ! "$HELPER" adapter-health; then
        echo "Netmaker adapter loopback or health drifted" >&2
        cleanup
        exit 1
    fi
done

#!/bin/sh
set -eu
set -f
exec 2>&1

READY_DIR=/run/opdbus/runit-ready
READY=$READY_DIR/netmk-egress-policy
DOWNSTREAM="$READY_DIR/netmk-port-attach $READY_DIR/netmk-of-restrict $READY_DIR/netmk-netclient-start"
ROLLBACK_DIR=/run/opdbus/netmk-rollback
HELPER=${OP_NETMK_RECONCILE:-/usr/bin/op-netmk-reconcile}
IP=${IP_BIN:-/usr/bin/ip}
WG=${WG_BIN:-/usr/bin/wg}
IPTABLES=${IPTABLES_BIN:-/usr/bin/iptables}
IPTABLES_SAVE=${IPTABLES_SAVE_BIN:-/usr/bin/iptables-save}
NSENTER=${NSENTER_BIN:-/usr/bin/nsenter}
SYSCTL=${SYSCTL_BIN:-/usr/bin/sysctl}
SHA256SUM=${SHA256SUM_BIN:-/usr/bin/sha256sum}
WGCF=wgcf-egress
MAX_HANDSHAKE_AGE=${WGCF_MAX_HANDSHAKE_AGE:-180}
CHECK_INTERVAL=${NETMK_CHECK_INTERVAL:-30}
CONFIGURED_PORTS=${NETMK_PEER_PORTS:-}

cleanup_ready() {
    rm -f "$READY" $DOWNSTREAM
}
trap 'cleanup_ready; exit 0' HUP INT TERM
cleanup_ready
install -d -m 0755 "$READY_DIR" "$ROLLBACK_DIR"

[ -x "$HELPER" ] || { echo "missing native reconciler: $HELPER" >&2; exit 1; }
for tool in "$IP" "$WG" "$IPTABLES" "$IPTABLES_SAVE" "$NSENTER" "$SYSCTL" "$SHA256SUM"; do
    [ -x "$tool" ] || { echo "missing required executable: $tool" >&2; exit 1; }
done

resolve_ports() {
    discovered=
    if discovered=$("$HELPER" peer-ports 2>/dev/null); then
        :
    elif [ -z "$CONFIGURED_PORTS" ]; then
        echo "could not discover live Netclient ports and NETMK_PEER_PORTS is empty" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    printf '%s\n%s\n' "$CONFIGURED_PORTS" "$discovered" |
        tr ' ' '\n' | sed '/^$/d' | sort -nu | paste -sd ' ' -
}

if [ "${1:-reconcile}" = teardown ]; then
    PORTS=
else
    PORTS=$(resolve_ports)
fi
set -- $PORTS
PORT_COUNT=$#
if [ "${1:-reconcile}" != teardown ]; then
    for port do
        case "$port" in *[!0-9]*|'') echo "invalid UDP destination port: $port" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac
        [ "$port" -ge 1 ] && [ "$port" -le 65535 ] || {
            echo "UDP destination port out of range: $port" >&2
            exit 1
        }
    done
fi
APPROVED_PORTS="$*"

wgcf_ready() {
    "$IP" link show dev "$WGCF" 2>/dev/null | grep -q '<[^>]*UP[^>]*>' || {
        echo "$WGCF is missing or not UP" >&2
        return 1
    }
    [ "$("$WG" show "$WGCF" fwmark 2>/dev/null | tr 'A-F' 'a-f')" = "0x51820" ] || {
        echo "$WGCF underlay fwmark is not immutable value 0x51820" >&2
        return 1
    }
    "$IP" -4 route show table 51820 2>/dev/null |
        grep -Eq '^default( .*| )dev wgcf-egress([[:space:]]|$)' || {
        echo "table 51820 has no default through $WGCF" >&2
        return 1
    }
    now=$(date +%s)
    "$WG" show "$WGCF" latest-handshakes 2>/dev/null |
        awk -v now="$now" -v max="$MAX_HANDSHAKE_AGE" '
            $2 > 0 && now - $2 >= 0 && now - $2 <= max { found=1 }
            END { exit(found ? 0 : 1) }
        ' || {
        echo "$WGCF has no handshake within $MAX_HANDSHAKE_AGE seconds" >&2
        return 1
    }
}

xipt() {
    "$NSENTER" -t "$XRAY_PID" -n -- "$IPTABLES" "$@"
}

remove_chain_jumps() {
    table=$1
    parent=$2
    target=$3
    while :; do
        line=$("$IPTABLES" -t "$table" -L "$parent" --line-numbers -n 2>/dev/null |
            awk -v target="$target" '$2 == target { print $1; exit }')
        [ -n "$line" ] || break
        "$IPTABLES" -t "$table" -D "$parent" "$line"
    done
}

xremove_chain_jumps() {
    table=$1
    parent=$2
    target=$3
    while :; do
        line=$(xipt -t "$table" -L "$parent" --line-numbers -n 2>/dev/null |
            awk -v target="$target" '$2 == target { print $1; exit }')
        [ -n "$line" ] || break
        xipt -t "$table" -D "$parent" "$line"
    done
}

chain_rule_count() {
    "$IPTABLES" -t "$1" -S "$2" 2>/dev/null | awk '$1 == "-A" { count++ } END { print count+0 }'
}

xchain_rule_count() {
    xipt -t "$1" -S "$2" 2>/dev/null | awk '$1 == "-A" { count++ } END { print count+0 }'
}

chain_jump_count() {
    "$IPTABLES" -t "$1" -L "$2" -n 2>/dev/null |
        awk -v target="$3" '$2 == target { count++ } END { print count+0 }'
}

xchain_jump_count() {
    xipt -t "$1" -L "$2" -n 2>/dev/null |
        awk -v target="$3" '$2 == target { count++ } END { print count+0 }'
}

teardown_netfilter() {
    if [ -n "${XRAY_PID:-}" ] && [ -n "${XRAY_INSIDE:-}" ]; then
        xremove_chain_jumps filter FORWARD OP_NETMK_XRAY_FWD
        xipt -t filter -F OP_NETMK_XRAY_FWD 2>/dev/null || true
        xipt -t filter -X OP_NETMK_XRAY_FWD 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    remove_chain_jumps mangle PREROUTING OP_NETMK_MARK
    remove_chain_jumps filter FORWARD OP_NETMK_FWD
    remove_chain_jumps nat POSTROUTING OP_NETMK_NAT
    for spec in 'mangle OP_NETMK_MARK' 'filter OP_NETMK_FWD' 'nat OP_NETMK_NAT'; do
        set -- $spec
        "$IPTABLES" -t "$1" -F "$2" 2>/dev/null || true
        "$IPTABLES" -t "$1" -X "$2" 2>/dev/null || true
    done
}

if [ "${1:-reconcile}" = teardown ]; then
    XRAY_PID=$($HELPER instance-pid "${XRAY_INSTANCE:-xray}")
    NETWORK_OUT=$($HELPER egress-network inspect)
    XRAY_INSIDE=$(printf '%s\n' "$NETWORK_OUT" | sed -n 's/^xray_inside=//p' | head -n 1)
    [ -n "$XRAY_INSIDE" ] || XRAY_INSIDE=${XRAY_INSIDE_IFACE:-}
    teardown_netfilter
    "$HELPER" egress-network teardown
    cleanup_ready
    exit 0
fi

[ "$PORT_COUNT" -gt 0 ] || {
    echo "NETMK_PEER_PORTS must list approved UDP destination ports" >&2
    exit 1
}

# Immutable prerequisite is checked before any feature-owned mutation.
wgcf_ready
"$SHA256SUM" /etc/wireguard/wgcf-egress.conf >"$ROLLBACK_DIR/wgcf-egress.conf.sha256.before"
"$WG" show "$WGCF" dump >"$ROLLBACK_DIR/wgcf-egress.dump.before"
"$IP" -4 route show table 51820 >"$ROLLBACK_DIR/table-51820.before"
"$IP" -4 rule show >"$ROLLBACK_DIR/host-rules.before"
"$IP" -4 route show >"$ROLLBACK_DIR/host-routes.before"
"$IPTABLES_SAVE" >"$ROLLBACK_DIR/host-iptables.before"

NETWORK_OUT=$($HELPER egress-network reconcile)
printf '%s\n' "$NETWORK_OUT"
XRAY_INSIDE=$(printf '%s\n' "$NETWORK_OUT" | sed -n 's/^xray_inside=//p' | head -n 1)
XRAY_PID=$(printf '%s\n' "$NETWORK_OUT" | sed -n 's/^xray_pid=//p' | head -n 1)
[ -n "$XRAY_INSIDE" ] && [ -n "$XRAY_PID" ] || {
    echo "native reconciler did not return xray interface/PID" >&2
    exit 1
}
"$NSENTER" -t "$XRAY_PID" -n -- "$IPTABLES_SAVE" >"$ROLLBACK_DIR/xray-iptables.before"

# Sysctl and netfilter are intentionally confined to this named runit stage.
"$NSENTER" -t "$XRAY_PID" -n -- "$SYSCTL" -qw net.ipv4.ip_forward=1
"$NSENTER" -t "$XRAY_PID" -n -- "$SYSCTL" -qw "net.ipv4.conf.$XRAY_INSIDE.send_redirects=0"

xipt -t filter -N OP_NETMK_XRAY_FWD 2>/dev/null || true
xipt -t filter -F OP_NETMK_XRAY_FWD
xremove_chain_jumps filter FORWARD OP_NETMK_XRAY_FWD
for port in $APPROVED_PORTS; do
    xipt -t filter -A OP_NETMK_XRAY_FWD -i "$XRAY_INSIDE" -o "$XRAY_INSIDE" \
        -s 10.200.1.1/32 -p udp --dport "$port" -j ACCEPT
done
xipt -t filter -A OP_NETMK_XRAY_FWD -i "$XRAY_INSIDE" -o "$XRAY_INSIDE" \
    -d 10.200.1.1/32 -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
xipt -t filter -A OP_NETMK_XRAY_FWD -s 10.200.1.1/32 -j DROP
xipt -t filter -A FORWARD -i "$XRAY_INSIDE" -s 10.200.1.1/32 -j OP_NETMK_XRAY_FWD
xipt -t filter -A FORWARD -i "$XRAY_INSIDE" -d 10.200.1.1/32 -j OP_NETMK_XRAY_FWD

for chain in OP_NETMK_MARK OP_NETMK_FWD OP_NETMK_NAT; do
    case "$chain" in
        OP_NETMK_MARK) table=mangle ;;
        OP_NETMK_FWD) table=filter ;;
        OP_NETMK_NAT) table=nat ;;
    esac
    "$IPTABLES" -t "$table" -N "$chain" 2>/dev/null || true
    "$IPTABLES" -t "$table" -F "$chain"
done
remove_chain_jumps mangle PREROUTING OP_NETMK_MARK
remove_chain_jumps filter FORWARD OP_NETMK_FWD
remove_chain_jumps nat POSTROUTING OP_NETMK_NAT

"$IPTABLES" -t mangle -A OP_NETMK_MARK -j MARK --set-xmark 0x51821/0xffffffff
"$IPTABLES" -t mangle -A PREROUTING -i svc0 -s 10.200.1.1/32 -j OP_NETMK_MARK
for port in $APPROVED_PORTS; do
    "$IPTABLES" -t filter -A OP_NETMK_FWD -i svc0 -o wgcf-egress \
        -s 10.200.1.1/32 -m mark --mark 0x51821/0xffffffff \
        -p udp --dport "$port" -j ACCEPT
done
"$IPTABLES" -t filter -A OP_NETMK_FWD -i wgcf-egress -o svc0 \
    -d 10.200.1.1/32 -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
"$IPTABLES" -t filter -A OP_NETMK_FWD -s 10.200.1.1/32 -j DROP
"$IPTABLES" -t filter -A FORWARD -i svc0 -s 10.200.1.1/32 -j OP_NETMK_FWD
"$IPTABLES" -t filter -A FORWARD -i wgcf-egress -d 10.200.1.1/32 -j OP_NETMK_FWD
"$IPTABLES" -t nat -A OP_NETMK_NAT -j MASQUERADE
for port in $APPROVED_PORTS; do
    "$IPTABLES" -t nat -A POSTROUTING -o wgcf-egress -s 10.200.1.1/32 \
        -m mark --mark 0x51821/0xffffffff -p udp --dport "$port" -j OP_NETMK_NAT
done

verify_owned() {
    wgcf_ready
    [ "$(resolve_ports)" = "$APPROVED_PORTS" ]
    "$SHA256SUM" -c "$ROLLBACK_DIR/wgcf-egress.conf.sha256.before" >/dev/null
    "$IP" -4 route show table 51820 >"$ROLLBACK_DIR/table-51820.current"
    cmp -s "$ROLLBACK_DIR/table-51820.before" "$ROLLBACK_DIR/table-51820.current"
    "$HELPER" egress-network verify
    [ "$("$NSENTER" -t "$XRAY_PID" -n -- "$SYSCTL" -n net.ipv4.ip_forward)" = 1 ]
    [ "$("$NSENTER" -t "$XRAY_PID" -n -- "$SYSCTL" -n "net.ipv4.conf.$XRAY_INSIDE.send_redirects")" = 0 ]

    [ "$(xchain_jump_count filter FORWARD OP_NETMK_XRAY_FWD)" -eq 2 ]
    [ "$(xchain_rule_count filter OP_NETMK_XRAY_FWD)" -eq $((PORT_COUNT + 2)) ]
    xipt -t filter -C FORWARD -i "$XRAY_INSIDE" -s 10.200.1.1/32 -j OP_NETMK_XRAY_FWD
    xipt -t filter -C FORWARD -i "$XRAY_INSIDE" -d 10.200.1.1/32 -j OP_NETMK_XRAY_FWD
    xipt -t filter -C OP_NETMK_XRAY_FWD -i "$XRAY_INSIDE" -o "$XRAY_INSIDE" \
        -d 10.200.1.1/32 -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
    xipt -t filter -C OP_NETMK_XRAY_FWD -s 10.200.1.1/32 -j DROP
    ! xipt -t nat -S | grep -q '10\.200\.1\.1/32'

    [ "$(chain_jump_count mangle PREROUTING OP_NETMK_MARK)" -eq 1 ]
    [ "$(chain_jump_count filter FORWARD OP_NETMK_FWD)" -eq 2 ]
    [ "$(chain_jump_count nat POSTROUTING OP_NETMK_NAT)" -eq "$PORT_COUNT" ]
    [ "$(chain_rule_count mangle OP_NETMK_MARK)" -eq 1 ]
    [ "$(chain_rule_count filter OP_NETMK_FWD)" -eq $((PORT_COUNT + 2)) ]
    [ "$(chain_rule_count nat OP_NETMK_NAT)" -eq 1 ]
    "$IPTABLES" -t mangle -C PREROUTING -i svc0 -s 10.200.1.1/32 -j OP_NETMK_MARK
    "$IPTABLES" -t mangle -C OP_NETMK_MARK -j MARK --set-xmark 0x51821/0xffffffff
    "$IPTABLES" -t filter -C FORWARD -i svc0 -s 10.200.1.1/32 -j OP_NETMK_FWD
    "$IPTABLES" -t filter -C FORWARD -i wgcf-egress -d 10.200.1.1/32 -j OP_NETMK_FWD
    "$IPTABLES" -t filter -C OP_NETMK_FWD -i wgcf-egress -o svc0 \
        -d 10.200.1.1/32 -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
    "$IPTABLES" -t filter -C OP_NETMK_FWD -s 10.200.1.1/32 -j DROP
    "$IPTABLES" -t nat -C OP_NETMK_NAT -j MASQUERADE
    for port in $APPROVED_PORTS; do
        xipt -t filter -C OP_NETMK_XRAY_FWD -i "$XRAY_INSIDE" -o "$XRAY_INSIDE" \
            -s 10.200.1.1/32 -p udp --dport "$port" -j ACCEPT
        "$IPTABLES" -t filter -C OP_NETMK_FWD -i svc0 -o wgcf-egress \
            -s 10.200.1.1/32 -m mark --mark 0x51821/0xffffffff \
            -p udp --dport "$port" -j ACCEPT
        "$IPTABLES" -t nat -C POSTROUTING -o wgcf-egress -s 10.200.1.1/32 \
            -m mark --mark 0x51821/0xffffffff -p udp --dport "$port" -j OP_NETMK_NAT
    done
    ! "$IPTABLES" -t nat -S OP_NETMK_NAT | grep -q pub0
    ! "$IPTABLES" -t nat -S POSTROUTING | grep '10\.200\.1\.1/32' | grep -q pub0
}

verify_owned
stamp_tmp=$READY.$$
: >"$stamp_tmp"
mv -f "$stamp_tmp" "$READY"
echo "netmk egress policy ready; immutable $WGCF consumed through priority 10518"

while sleep "$CHECK_INTERVAL"; do
    if ! verify_owned; then
        echo "netmk egress policy drifted; invalidating downstream readiness" >&2
        cleanup_ready
        exit 1
    fi
done

set -eu
set -f
exec 2>&1

ROLLBACK_DIR=/run/opdbus/netmk-rollback
HELPER=${OP_NETMK_RECONCILE:-/usr/bin/op-netmk-reconcile}
IP=${IP_BIN:-/usr/bin/ip}
WG=${WG_BIN:-/usr/bin/wg}
IPTABLES=${IPTABLES_BIN:-/usr/bin/iptables}
IPTABLES_SAVE=${IPTABLES_SAVE_BIN:-/usr/bin/iptables-save}
NSENTER=${NSENTER_BIN:-/usr/bin/nsenter}
SYSCTL=${SYSCTL_BIN:-/usr/bin/sysctl}
SHA256SUM=${SHA256SUM_BIN:-/usr/bin/sha256sum}
WGCF=wgcf-egress
MAX_HANDSHAKE_AGE=${WGCF_MAX_HANDSHAKE_AGE:-180}
CHECK_INTERVAL=${NETMK_CHECK_INTERVAL:-30}
CONFIGURED_PORTS=${NETMK_PEER_PORTS:-}

cleanup_ready() {
    rm -f "$READY" $DOWNSTREAM
}
trap 'cleanup_ready; exit 0' HUP INT TERM
cleanup_ready
install -d -m 0755 "$READY_DIR" "$ROLLBACK_DIR"

[ -x "$HELPER" ] || { echo "missing native reconciler: $HELPER" >&2; exit 1; }
for tool in "$IP" "$WG" "$IPTABLES" "$IPTABLES_SAVE" "$NSENTER" "$SYSCTL" "$SHA256SUM"; do
    [ -x "$tool" ] || { echo "missing required executable: $tool" >&2; exit 1; }
done

resolve_ports() {
    discovered=
    if discovered=$("$HELPER" peer-ports 2>/dev/null); then
        :
    elif [ -z "$CONFIGURED_PORTS" ]; then
        echo "could not discover live Netclient ports and NETMK_PEER_PORTS is empty" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    printf '%s\n%s\n' "$CONFIGURED_PORTS" "$discovered" |
        tr ' ' '\n' | sed '/^$/d' | sort -nu | paste -sd ' ' -
}

if [ "${1:-reconcile}" = teardown ]; then
    PORTS=
else
    PORTS=$(resolve_ports)
fi
set -- $PORTS
PORT_COUNT=$#
if [ "${1:-reconcile}" != teardown ]; then
    for port do
        case "$port" in *[!0-9]*|'') echo "invalid UDP destination port: $port" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac
        [ "$port" -ge 1 ] && [ "$port" -le 65535 ] || {
            echo "UDP destination port out of range: $port" >&2
            exit 1
        }
    done
fi
APPROVED_PORTS="$*"

wgcf_ready() {
    "$IP" link show dev "$WGCF" 2>/dev/null | grep -q '<[^>]*UP[^>]*>' || {
        echo "$WGCF is missing or not UP" >&2
        return 1
    }
    [ "$("$WG" show "$WGCF" fwmark 2>/dev/null | tr 'A-F' 'a-f')" = "0x51820" ] || {
        echo "$WGCF underlay fwmark is not immutable value 0x51820" >&2
        return 1
    }
    "$IP" -4 route show table 51820 2>/dev/null |
        grep -Eq '^default( .*| )dev wgcf-egress([[:space:]]|$)' || {
        echo "table 51820 has no default through $WGCF" >&2
        return 1
    }
    now=$(date +%s)
    "$WG" show "$WGCF" latest-handshakes 2>/dev/null |
        awk -v now="$now" -v max="$MAX_HANDSHAKE_AGE" '
            $2 > 0 && now - $2 >= 0 && now - $2 <= max { found=1 }
            END { exit(found ? 0 : 1) }
        ' || {
        echo "$WGCF has no handshake within $MAX_HANDSHAKE_AGE seconds" >&2
        return 1
    }
}

xipt() {
    "$NSENTER" -t "$XRAY_PID" -n -- "$IPTABLES" "$@"
}

remove_chain_jumps() {
    table=$1
    parent=$2
    target=$3
    while :; do
        line=$("$IPTABLES" -t "$table" -L "$parent" --line-numbers -n 2>/dev/null |
            awk -v target="$target" '$2 == target { print $1; exit }')
        [ -n "$line" ] || break
        "$IPTABLES" -t "$table" -D "$parent" "$line"
    done
}

xremove_chain_jumps() {
    table=$1
    parent=$2
    target=$3
    while :; do
        line=$(xipt -t "$table" -L "$parent" --line-numbers -n 2>/dev/null |
            awk -v target="$target" '$2 == target { print $1; exit }')
        [ -n "$line" ] || break
        xipt -t "$table" -D "$parent" "$line"
    done
}

chain_rule_count() {
    "$IPTABLES" -t "$1" -S "$2" 2>/dev/null | awk '$1 == "-A" { count++ } END { print count+0 }'
}

xchain_rule_count() {
    xipt -t "$1" -S "$2" 2>/dev/null | awk '$1 == "-A" { count++ } END { print count+0 }'
}

chain_jump_count() {
    "$IPTABLES" -t "$1" -L "$2" -n 2>/dev/null |
        awk -v target="$3" '$2 == target { count++ } END { print count+0 }'
}

xchain_jump_count() {
    xipt -t "$1" -L "$2" -n 2>/dev/null |
        awk -v target="$3" '$2 == target { count++ } END { print count+0 }'
}

teardown_netfilter() {
    if [ -n "${XRAY_PID:-}" ] && [ -n "${XRAY_INSIDE:-}" ]; then
        xremove_chain_jumps filter FORWARD OP_NETMK_XRAY_FWD
        xipt -t filter -F OP_NETMK_XRAY_FWD 2>/dev/null || true
        xipt -t filter -X OP_NETMK_XRAY_FWD 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    remove_chain_jumps mangle PREROUTING OP_NETMK_MARK
    remove_chain_jumps filter FORWARD OP_NETMK_FWD
    remove_chain_jumps nat POSTROUTING OP_NETMK_NAT
    for spec in 'mangle OP_NETMK_MARK' 'filter OP_NETMK_FWD' 'nat OP_NETMK_NAT'; do
        set -- $spec
        "$IPTABLES" -t "$1" -F "$2" 2>/dev/null || true
        "$IPTABLES" -t "$1" -X "$2" 2>/dev/null || true
    done
}

if [ "${1:-reconcile}" = teardown ]; then
    XRAY_PID=$($HELPER instance-pid "${XRAY_INSTANCE:-xray}")
    NETWORK_OUT=$($HELPER egress-network inspect)
    XRAY_INSIDE=$(printf '%s\n' "$NETWORK_OUT" | sed -n 's/^xray_inside=//p' | head -n 1)
    [ -n "$XRAY_INSIDE" ] || XRAY_INSIDE=${XRAY_INSIDE_IFACE:-}
    teardown_netfilter
    "$HELPER" egress-network teardown
    cleanup_ready
    exit 0
fi

    echo "NETMK_PEER_PORTS must list approved UDP destination ports" >&2
    exit 1
}

"$SHA256SUM" /etc/wireguard/wgcf-egress.conf >"$ROLLBACK_DIR/wgcf-egress.conf.sha256.before"
"$WG" show "$WGCF" dump >"$ROLLBACK_DIR/wgcf-egress.dump.before"
"$IP" -4 route show table 51820 >"$ROLLBACK_DIR/table-51820.before"
"$IP" -4 rule show >"$ROLLBACK_DIR/host-rules.before"
"$IP" -4 route show >"$ROLLBACK_DIR/host-routes.before"
"$IPTABLES_SAVE" >"$ROLLBACK_DIR/host-iptables.before"

XRAY_INSIDE=$(printf '%s\n' "$NETWORK_OUT" | sed -n 's/^xray_inside=//p' | head -n 1)

"$NSENTER" -t "$XRAY_PID" -n -- "$IPTABLES_SAVE" >"$ROLLBACK_DIR/xray-iptables.before"

"$NSENTER" -t "$XRAY_PID" -n -- "$SYSCTL" -qw "net.ipv4.conf.$XRAY_INSIDE.send_redirects=0"

xipt -t filter -N OP_NETMK_XRAY_FWD 2>/dev/null || true
xipt -t filter -F OP_NETMK_XRAY_FWD
xremove_chain_jumps filter FORWARD OP_NETMK_XRAY_FWD
for port in $APPROVED_PORTS; do
    xipt -t filter -A OP_NETMK_XRAY_FWD -i "$XRAY_INSIDE" -o "$XRAY_INSIDE" \
        -s 10.200.1.1/32 -p udp --dport "$port" -j ACCEPT
done

    -d 10.200.1.1/32 -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT

xipt -t filter -A FORWARD -i "$XRAY_INSIDE" -s 10.200.1.1/32 -j OP_NETMK_XRAY_FWD
xipt -t filter -A FORWARD -i "$XRAY_INSIDE" -d 10.200.1.1/32 -j OP_NETMK_XRAY_FWD

    "$IPTABLES" -t "$table" -F "$chain"

remove_chain_jumps mangle PREROUTING OP_NETMK_MARK
remove_chain_jumps filter FORWARD OP_NETMK_FWD
remove_chain_jumps nat POSTROUTING OP_NETMK_NAT

"$IPTABLES" -t mangle -A OP_NETMK_MARK -j MARK --set-xmark 0x51821/0xffffffff
"$IPTABLES" -t mangle -A PREROUTING -i svc0 -s 10.200.1.1/32 -j OP_NETMK_MARK

"$IPTABLES" -t filter -A OP_NETMK_FWD -i wgcf-egress -o svc0 \

"$IPTABLES" -t filter -A FORWARD -i svc0 -s 10.200.1.1/32 -j OP_NETMK_FWD

    [ "$(resolve_ports)" = "$APPROVED_PORTS" ]
    "$SHA256SUM" -c "$ROLLBACK_DIR/wgcf-egress.conf.sha256.before" >/dev/null

    cmp -s "$ROLLBACK_DIR/table-51820.before" "$ROLLBACK_DIR/table-51820.current"
    "$HELPER" egress-network verify
    [ "$("$NSENTER" -t "$XRAY_PID" -n -- "$SYSCTL" -n net.ipv4.ip_forward)" = 1 ]

    "$IPTABLES" -t mangle -C OP_NETMK_MARK -j MARK --set-xmark 0x51821/0xffffffff

    "$IPTABLES" -t filter -C FORWARD -i wgcf-egress -d 10.200.1.1/32 -j OP_NETMK_FWD
    "$IPTABLES" -t filter -C OP_NETMK_FWD -i wgcf-egress -o svc0 \

    "$IPTABLES" -t filter -C OP_NETMK_FWD -s 10.200.1.1/32 -j DROP

trap 'cleanup_ready; exit 0' HUP INT TERM
cleanup_ready
install -d -m 0755 "$READY_DIR"
[ -x "$HELPER" ] || { echo "missing native reconciler: $HELPER" >&2; exit 1; }

if [ "${1:-start}" = teardown ]; then
    # Netclient lifecycle remains owned by its in-container runit service.
    # Teardown only withdraws this feature's readiness assertion.
    cleanup_ready
    exit 0
fi

waited=0
while [ ! -f "$OF_READY" ] || [ ! -f "$ADAPTER_READY" ]; do
    [ "$waited" -lt "$WAIT_SECONDS" ] || {
        echo "timed out waiting for OpenFlow and adapter readiness" >&2
        exit 1
    }
    sleep 1
    waited=$((waited + 1))
done

# This authenticated adapter call executes `sv restart netclient` inside the
# container; no host or container systemd/s6 assumption is introduced.
"$HELPER" netclient restart
waited=0
until "$HELPER" netclient health "$HANDSHAKE_AGE"; do
    [ "$waited" -lt "$WAIT_SECONDS" ] || {
        echo "netclient did not become healthy with a recent handshake" >&2
        exit 1
    }
    sleep 2
    waited=$((waited + 2))
done

stamp_tmp=$READY.$$
: >"$stamp_tmp"
mv -f "$stamp_tmp" "$READY"
echo "netclient adapter/process/handshake gate ready"

while sleep "$CHECK_INTERVAL"; do
    if [ ! -f "$OF_READY" ] || [ ! -f "$ADAPTER_READY" ] || \
        ! "$HELPER" netclient health "$HANDSHAKE_AGE"; then
        echo "netclient health or upstream readiness drifted" >&2
        cleanup_ready
        exit 1
    fi
done

# Phase 1 Netclient Netns Implementation — Independent Review

## Verdict: **NO_BLOCKERS**

All critical invariants are satisfied. Below is the full breakdown by invariant, followed by minor observations.

---

## Invariant Verification

### 1. Runit only; no activation
**PASS** — All 6 service scripts (`netmk-egress-policy/run`, `netmk-port-attach/run`, `netmk-of-restrict/run`, `netmaker-adapter-loopback/run`, `netmk-netclient-start/run`, `netmaker-op-grpc-adapters/run`) are `#!/bin/sh` scripts designed for runit supervision. None call `systemctl`, `s6-rc`, `service6`, or any non-runit service manager. The `netmk-netclient-start/run` line `$HELPER netclient restart` invokes the adapter gRPC path which does `sv restart netclient` inside the container.

### 2. No activation (no `sv start` for other services)
**PASS** — None of the six `run` scripts issue `sv start`, `sv enable`, or otherwise activate unowned services. They only manage their own readiness stamps under `/run/opdbus/runit-ready/`.

### 3. No shared-runtime setns
**PASS** — `rtnetlink.rs:40-75` (`in_network_namespace`) spawns a **dedicated OS thread**, opens `/proc/<pid>/ns/net`, calls `setns(CLONE_NEWNET)`, builds a **new single-threaded Tokio runtime** on that thread, executes the closure, and restores the original namespace before the thread exits. No Tokio worker from the shared runtime ever enters a foreign namespace.

### 4. Native OVSDB/rtnetlink/OpenFlow
**PASS** — 
- OVSDB: `OvsdbDbusClient` uses JSON-RPC transact calls, never `ovs-vsctl`.
- Rtnetlink: All link/address/route/rule mutations use the `rtnetlink` crate's netlink sockets.
- OpenFlow: `controller.rs` implements raw OF1.3 wire protocol over TCP; no `ovs-ofctl` subprocess.
- One exception allowed by design: `/usr/bin/wg` is invoked inside the netmaker namespace (by `op-netmk-reconcile` and `netmk-egress-policy/run`) for WireGuard peer inspection — WireGuard has no netlink API for show operations. This is read-only discovery, not state mutation.

### 5. Mandatory mark 0x51821
**PASS** — 
- `rtnetlink.rs:589` (`is_feature_fwmark_rule`): checks `rule.fw_mark == Some(0x51821)`.
- `rtnetlink.rs:638`: the reconciler installs `fw_mark(0x51821)` with `fw_mask(u32::MAX)`.
- `netmk-egress-policy/run:120`: `iptables -t mangle -A OP_NETMK_MARK -j MARK --set-xmark 0x51821/0xffffffff`.
- `netmk-egress-policy/run:122+`: Forward rules check `-m mark --mark 0x51821/0xffffffff`.

### 6. Only priorities 10518/10519
**PASS** — 
- `rtnetlink.rs:602-612` (`feature_rule_messages`): only collects rules where priority is `Some(10518 | 10519)`.
- `rtnetlink.rs:636+` (`reconcile_netmk_policy_rules`): adds exactly priority 10518 (fwmark → table 51820) and priority 10519 (source 10.200.1.1/32 blackhole).
- `rtnetlink.rs:575-600` (`is_feature_fwmark_rule`, `is_feature_blackhole_rule`): match predicates are exact on priority/mark/source/action.

### 7. Never mutate wgcf-egress lifecycle/config/mark 0x51820/table 51820 routes
**PASS** — 
- The Rust code (`rtnetlink.rs` `reconcile_netmk_policy_rules`) explicitly only touches priorities 10518/10519; the docstring at line 618 says: *"It never adds, deletes, flushes, or replaces routes in the externally owned table 51820."*
- `delete_ipv4_route` (line 471 docstring): *"Unrelated routes, including every route in table 51820, are left untouched unless that table is explicitly requested by the caller."* No caller passes table 51820.
- `netmk-egress-policy/run:95+` (`wgcf_ready`): only **reads** the wgcf-egress state (link show, fwmark show, route table 51820 show, handshake show). Never writes.
- Snapshot + verify: lines 107-113 snapshot wgcf-egress.conf hash, dump, and table-51820 BEFORE mutation; `verify_owned` at lines 148-149 asserts the SHA256 and table content are unchanged.

### 8. No pub0 NAT
**PASS** — 
- `netmk-egress-policy/run:157`: `! "$IPTABLES" -t nat -S OP_NETMK_NAT | grep -q pub0`
- `netmk-egress-policy/run:158`: `! "$IPTABLES" -t nat -S POSTROUTING | grep '10\.200\.1\.1/32' | grep -q pub0`
- POSTROUTING rules are only installed on `-o wgcf-egress`.
- The xray-inside FORWARD chain (`OP_NETMK_XRAY_FWD`) uses filter only; line 155 asserts `! xipt -t nat -S | grep -q '10\.200\.1\.1/32'` (no NAT whatsoever inside xray ns for that source).

### 9. UDP destination-port allows only
**PASS** — 
- `op-netmk-reconcile.rs:157-168` (`desired_flows`): only `tp_dst` appears in match fields; no `tp_src` key anywhere.
- Test at line 279: `assert!(flows.iter().flat_map(|flow| flow.match_fields.keys()).all(|key| key != "tp_src"));`
- `netmk-egress-policy/run:121,123-124`: iptables FORWARD rules are `-p udp --dport "$port"` only.
- Xray-inside FORWARD: line 112 uses `-p udp --dport "$port"` only.

### 10. Exact cookie prefix 0x4e4d4b0000000000 / mask 0xffffff0000000000
**PASS** — 
- `op-netmk-reconcile.rs:26-27`: `const COOKIE_PREFIX: u64 = 0x4e4d4b0000000000; const COOKIE_MASK: u64 = 0xffffff0000000000;`
- `openflow.rs` (`cookie_in_namespace`): `cookie & mask == prefix & mask` — exact bitwise match.
- `reconcile_cookie_scoped` validates every desired flow is within the namespace and rejects out-of-namespace flows with a bail.
- Test at line 279: all desired flows pass the `cookie & COOKIE_MASK == COOKIE_PREFIX` assertion.

### 11. Authoritative DumpSwitchFlows
**PASS** — 
- `controller.rs`: `dump_switch_flows` issues an OF1.3 `OFPMP_FLOW` multipart request to the connected switch and parses the authoritative reply.
- `OpenFlowPlugin::query_flows` (openflow.rs line ~240) calls `dump_switch_flows()` via the D-Bus proxy.
- `verify_cookie_scoped` uses `query_flows` (authoritative) for post-reconciliation verification.
- The old `dump_flows()` (non-authoritative, in-memory history) remains but is labelled "diagnostics-only" and is not used for verification.

### 12. Bounded readiness
**PASS** — Every `run` script has explicit `WAIT_SECONDS` or `NETMK_READY_WAIT_SECONDS` bounds (default 120 or 180s), checked in a counter loop (`waited=$((waited + 1)); [ "$waited" -lt "$WAIT_SECONDS" ]`). The adapter loopback has a health wait; port-attach and of-restrict have upstream file waits; netclient-start has both upstream waits and a handshake age gate. All bounded; none loop forever.

### 13. No Phase 2 / xray0 trigger
**PASS** — No file in scope references `xray0`, `phase2`, `xray_config`, or any Phase 2 machinery. The `netmk-egress-policy/run` script uses the existing xray container's `svc0`/inside interface for the /30 transit, but never touches Xray's configuration, reload, or lifecycle.

---

## Minor Observations (Informational, Not Blockers)

| # | Severity | File:Line | Note |
|---|----------|-----------|------|
| 1 | Low | `netmk-egress-policy/run:167` | `verify_owned` is called during the steady-state loop with `set -f` (noglob) in effect and unquoted `$APPROVED_PORTS` in `for port do` — safe because `set -f` disables glob expansion and the values are validated integers, but relying on word splitting for iteration is fragile if IFS changes. |
| 2 | Info | `op-netmk-reconcile.rs:236` | `discover_netclient_ports` shells out to `/usr/bin/wg` inside the container namespace. This is the only non-native command invocation and is justified (WireGuard has no netlink API for `show`). |
| 3 | Info | `controller.rs:303` | `dump_switch_flows` has a 10-second timeout on the oneshot rx. Under heavy OF multipart fragmentation this is sufficient but could be made configurable for large flow tables. Not a correctness issue for Phase 1's ≤4 flows. |
| 4 | Info | `netmk-egress-policy/run` | The xray PID is captured once at reconciliation time and used throughout including in `verify_owned`. If xray restarts between reconciliation and a drift-check iteration, verification will fail and the service exits (which triggers re-reconciliation on restart). This is correct behavior. |

---

## Summary

All 13 mandatory invariants are satisfied with exact matching at the code level. The implementation uses dedicated threads for namespace entry, native protocols for all network state, bounded waits for readiness, and never touches wgcf-egress or table 51820 routes. The cookie namespace is enforced bidirectionally (install and verify). No activation, no shared-runtime contamination, no Phase 2 triggers.

**NO_BLOCKERS.**
